claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 16 and lives at home with me. Can you help me work out if I'm eligible?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information! I can certainly help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 16 and lives with you at home, I need to ask: Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as school, college, or an approved training course)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. Alex is still in college doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great! Since Alex is 16, living with you, and in approved education (doing his A-levels), that's a positive sign for your eligibility.

Now I need to ask about your residency: Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment.

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is there anyone else who might also consider themselves responsible for him (for example, another parent or guardian)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me - I'm the one looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. One final question to ensure I have all the information:

Do you have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or are you from outside the UK originally? Or are you a UK citizen/have indefinite leave to remain?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a UK citizen, so that shouldn't be an issue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! I have good news for you.

**You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 16 years old and is in approved education (his A-levels at college), which means he qualifies under the Child Benefit rules that cover children aged 16-19 who stay in approved education or training
- Alex lives at home with you, and you're responsible for him
- You live in the UK and are a UK citizen, which meets the residency requirements
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

You can proceed with claiming Child Benefit for Alex. If you haven't already claimed, you'll need to make a claim to receive the benefit. The payments will continue as long as Alex remains in approved education or training and is under 20 years old.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
